cohort: 30 patients who underwent emergency obstetric hysterectomies between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2019 at the Bafoussam Regional Hospital (BRH)
finding: The prevalence of emergency obstetric hysterectomy (EOH) was high (3.75 per 1000 deliveries), with no differences in sociodemographic profile, risk factors, or indications between caesarean and postpartum hysterectomy groups, but postpartum hysterectomy had a higher risk of sepsis.
